patch_summary: The core #359 traversal was already guarded in this snapshot (Directory.read realpath+commonpath check, tests, changelog). Found and fixed the remaining gap: attacker-controlled absolute hrefs on an incomparable path (e.g. different Windows drive/UNC) made os.path.commonpath raise ValueError instead of the documented OSError. Added regression test test_read_rejects_uncomparable_path_as_oserror (committed alone as 55ca08e; failed pre-fix with ValueError), then wrapped the commonpath check in try/except ValueError failing closed with OSError (committed alone as a76e9d4). Full suite: 171 passed, 1 failed — the single failure (test_html_encoding) is pre-existing on the untouched baseline and unrelated; ruff check passes on both changed files.
root_cause: Directory.read's containment check called os.path.commonpath without handling ValueError, which it raises for incomparable paths (different drives/UNC on Windows). Attacker-controlled manifest hrefs could thus trigger an undocumented exception type from the security boundary instead of failing closed with OSError.
